what_happened: A job that changed build slots had passed verification. Another job then landed first, so the passed job went stale because main moved under it. The the person running Athena had already lifted a pause and tried a retry, but Athena refuses to retry stale jobs, so neither step worked. The the person running Athena then queued a "retry-on-new-base" item by hand. It re-verifies the work on the new base, which docs/decisions.md named as the response to stale landings. The the person running Athena specified the design of that path in detail.
cause: The parallel-jobs feature shipped without the follow-through its own decision record called for. Landings in parallel make main move under verified jobs as a matter of course. The decision record said re-verification on the new base was the answer, but no command or drain step implemented it. The retry command also treats "stale" as a terminal state, so the lifecycle has no way out of it. Nothing compared the decisions file with the commands that exist to see whether each named trigger had a mechanism.
prevention: Add a stale-to-reverify transition. When a verified job's base is no longer main's tip, Athena automatically (or through a documented retry) rebases or replays the job on the new base. It re-runs the checks and the verifier there, and reuses the earlier verdict only if the diff is unchanged. The drain should run this itself when it finds a stale job, and retry should accept stale jobs and report the mode and expected cost first. That covers every case where main changes under verified work.
proposed_request: Make stale jobs recoverable without the person running Athena action. Outcome: when a job has passed verification but main has since moved, Athena moves it onto the new base and re-verifies it there, and the job lands if the checks and the verifier pass. Requirements: (1) `athena retry` accepts a stale job and shows beforehand whether it will rebuild or resume, and the expected cost. (2) The queue drain does this automatically for stale jobs, within the job budget, and records the new base and the verdict. (3) If the new base conflicts with the job's diff, the job ends in a clear needs-human state with the conflicting files named, not a refusal. (4) Update the stale-landing decision in docs/decisions.md to match. Acceptance: a test with two parallel jobs where the first lands and the second goes stale shows the second re-verified on the new base and landed by the drain without a manual command; a test with a conflicting diff shows the needs-human state. Also cover the default serial path (max_concurrency = 1).
